summaries.summary: Unity Gateway (formerly AI Gateway, Unity AI Gateway and Mosaic AI Gateway) is Databricks' GA governance layer, built on Unity Catalog, that fronts system.ai Foundation Models, BYOK external providers, MCP services and skills as Unity Catalog securables. Callers need EXECUTE plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA; CREATE SERVICE and MANAGE govern creation and configuration. It offers rate limits (HTTP 429), fallbacks, budgets and guardrails (service policies, Beta), with models queried at /ai-gateway/mlflow/v1 using names like system.ai.<model>.

A Unity Gateway MCP service is one of Databricks Unity Gateway's five object types, registering an external Streamable HTTP MCP server backed by a Unity Catalog HTTP connection. Registering needs CREATE SERVICE on the schema plus CREATE CONNECTION or USE CONNECTION, via the UI or the Unity Catalog mcp-services API. Agents then call it on the workspace /ai-gateway/mcp-services/<catalog>.<schema>.<service> route; Genie, Databricks Apps and Unity Catalog entity sources cannot be registered this way.

A Unity Gateway model provider service is Databricks' object for an external model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or Amazon Bedrock, including Bedrock Mantle) with centrally managed bring-your-own-key credentials; it replaces the older external models. The provider API key can be backed by a Unity Catalog secret, keeping keys out of agent code. A price multiplier can adjust spend estimates to reflect negotiated provider rates.

A Unity Gateway model service is a Databricks Unity Catalog object that routes to one or more models with traffic splitting and fallbacks. Callers need EXECUTE on the service plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA; all account users have EXECUTE on system.ai by default, revocable at schema level. Queries run against the service owner's privileges, so the owner needs EXECUTE on every destination including fallbacks, and managing system.ai needs metastore admin or MANAGE.

USE AI FUNCTIONS is the Snowflake account privilege required to call Cortex AI Functions, introduced 2026-02-20, with per-function USE AI FUNCTION <name> privileges GA since 2026-05-13. It is granted to PUBLIC by default and managed by ACCOUNTADMIN, who can revoke it from PUBLIC to restrict access. Under Restricted Caller's Rights it must be granted to both the session role and the service or application owner role.

USERADMIN is a Snowflake system role holding the CREATE USER and CREATE ROLE privileges, and Snowflake recommends it be used to create custom roles. In a least-privilege agent setup, USERADMIN creates the agent's user and role, while SECURITYADMIN or the object owner grants the privileges.

Vertex AI is Google Cloud's AI platform, renamed Agent Platform (part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, alongside Agent Runtime) on 2026-04-22, with old links redirecting. Unlike the Gemini API it authenticates with Cloud service accounts and IAM rather than API keys, and it is the option to use when data residency is required. The google-genai SDK targets it via genai.Client(vertexai=True, project, location), and the Apps Script Vertex AI advanced service is GA.

vertexai.allowedModels is a Google Cloud organization policy constraint restricting which models can be used on Agent Platform (Vertex AI), set by an Organization Policy Administrator at organization, folder or project level, where an explicit deny overrides an allow. Entries take the form publishers/PUBLISHER/models/MODEL:ACTION with predict, deploy or tune, with no wildcards and at most 500 values. Ask clients on day one about such restrictions alongside VPC-SC perimeter membership.

VPC Service Controls is Google Cloud's perimeter service that blocks API access across a boundary, refined by Access Context Manager access levels, ingress and egress rules (preferred over bridges) and dry-run mode. Its perimeter covers Agent Platform generative AI, inference, tuning, Vector Search, Agent Runtime and sandboxes, and Agent Gateway enforces it with ALL_TRAFFIC egress for deployments created after 2026-09-08. Agent Identity ingress and egress rule support was in Preview.

Work IQ is Microsoft's workplace intelligence layer for agents, GA since 2026-06-16, offering chat, context and tools over Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data via A2A, remote and local MCP, and REST. A tenant admin must enable it; it supports delegated on-behalf-of auth only (no app-only), with admin-consented scopes WorkIQAgent.Ask, WorkIQ.Act and WorkIQ.Read. Usage is billed per use in Copilot Credits, even for Copilot-licensed users.

Work IQ Dev Tools (wiqd) is Microsoft's preview CLI (v0.26.0) for building Microsoft 365 Copilot plugins and declarative agents, not custom engine agents, and is now the focus of the Copilot extensibility landing page. Users sign in with wiqd auth login --interactive, and commands include wiqd doctor, agent add action, agent validate, agent provision and an alpha plugin tree.

The Work IQ MCP server is Microsoft's GA remote MCP endpoint within the Work IQ API, recommended instead of the legacy per-workload Microsoft-hosted MCP servers; MCP clients discover its Entra auth through the oauth-protected-resource well-known path. It offers 10 generic tools over Graph-style resource paths (such as fetch, create_entity, ask and preview retrieve) plus get_schema and search_paths for discovery. Microsoft provides quickstarts for GitHub Copilot CLI and Foundry.

Workflow Builder is Google's Gemini Enterprise no-code and low-code builder for chat agents and scheduled multi-step workflows, formerly Agent Designer and GA under its new name since 2026-09-03. It can import existing A2A and ADK agents and connects to Microsoft Teams, Notion and Salesforce. Creating agents needs roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (or per-app grants with agentspaceRestrictedUser at project level) plus a Gemini Enterprise license.

Workforce Identity Federation is Google Cloud IAM's way for users from any OIDC or SAML 2.0 IdP (Entra ID, AD FS, Okta) to sign in without being copied into Cloud Identity, using organization-level workforce pools. Gemini Enterprise supports it for third-party-only setups: create the pool in global, map google.subject to lowercase email, and filter Entra group claims (150 for SAML, 200 for OIDC). Token exchange defaults to 1,000 requests per minute per organization; SCIM status is unconfirmed.

Workload Identity Federation is Google Cloud IAM's keyless way for external workloads (AWS, Azure/Entra ID, GitHub, GitLab, Kubernetes, any OIDC or SAML 2.0 IdP) to get Google credentials through pools, providers and STS token exchange. Mappings require google.subject, and principal identifiers use the project number. Google recommends granting roles directly to principal or principalSet identifiers, though some APIs need service account impersonation via roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser; creating pools needs roles/iam.workloadIdentityPoolAdmin.

xAI Grok is xAI's model family offered in OCI Generative AI, currently listing Grok 4.7, Grok 4.6, Grok 4.3, Grok 4.20 and Grok 4.20 Multi-Agent, with priority processing for Grok 4.20 and 4.3 since 2026-10-14. Because Grok is hosted by xAI, calls leave OCI. xAI models and tools on the OCI Responses API are US-only (Ashburn, Chicago, Phoenix).
